findings: Five active-audio cases using the original multi-track container lack an initial snapshot and log buffer deadlock prevented. Three no-audio cases produce a paused picture. Dummy audio also reproduces the original failure, but the plain one-audio/no-subtitle Matroska succeeds with WASAPI. Audio alone is not a sufficient cause.

Three remux controls (all tracks, two audio/no subtitles, one audio/two subtitles) start paused successfully with WASAPI. All1500 compressed video packets match the original; all video PTS shift21ms. Track count alone is not sufficient either. Container timing/layout is the next factor to isolate; this does not yet prove the exact cause or blame the audio driver.

The original-container subtitle-enabled controls show ENGLISH MIDDLE CUE after a25s request, then no subtitle after a5s backward request. The remux subtitle controls lack the middle cue too. All six subtitle-enabled controls lose text after the backward request and explicit external-track selection while paused, then render the external first cue after resume.
externalSelection: Adding external SRT with the public API select flag true leaves manually chosen Finnish selected. Explicit selection chooses Track3; sticky track-ID precedence needs tracing before a policy repair.
visualInspection: The WASAPI snapshots were directly inspected: seek-middle-paused shows ENGLISH MIDDLE CUE, seek-first-paused is plain gray, external-after-resume shows EXTERNAL FIRST CUE. Pixel counts corroborate presence/absence, not text recognition or arbitrary subtitle correctness.
scope: Twelve owned native LibVLC runs with actual Matroska/H264/AAC/SRT media, vdummy display and the native window provider named window. No wdummy/headless-window claim: the first unsupported --window=wdummy attempt is preserved as setup failure.

All twelve processes stop/release and exit0 with source/runtime/producer identities unchanged. Each retains one window-closed diagnostic verified at vout teardown before instance exit; five retain the startup error. Cache-missing, subtitle-codec fallback, size and occasional lateness warnings stay in original logs.

A snapshot call returning0 queues a request. The five missing initial files were unavailable during the two-second wait after one-second paused settling; files that appear later after resume are not initial-paused evidence and are excluded from the55 qualified snapshot artifacts.

Native get_time output-clock readback can remain stale while paused. Requested25s/5s values name operations, not exact frame-PTS acceptance. This investigation does not replace the earlier Qt pending-seek repair or native color-frame regression.

The native worker/header/layout/source inputs are recorded against existing source-r4 and GUI716862a1/Core4422/WASAPI4e4e. No production source or installed dependency changes in this investigation; no independent compiler provenance beyond earlier build receipts is invented.

R5 failed before initialization because window is not a command-line option. R5b executed media/Stop/release but failed report finalization on a missing Python import; its incomplete original receipt stays unchanged. R5c corrects the producer and adds explicit external-track selection. These are test-producer failures, not additional app crashes.
No whole workflow, exact target-frame timestamp, physical audibility, all formats, real service, Windows10, design/accessibility/DPI or beta/package acceptance.
